question: to the Commission Geadis Geadi (ECR) Subject:

Recently, there has been increased diplomatic momentum with regard to the Cyprus issue, with UN Secretary-General António Guterres visiting Cyprus with the aim of resuming negotiations, which have remained at a standstill since the breakdown of the Crans-Montana talks. The European Union and the European acquis are founded on the principles of equality, nondiscrimination and respect for human rights for all people, as enshrined in the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. At the same time, the Charter of the United Nations, and in particular Article 1(3) thereof, provides for the promotion of ‘respect for human rights and for fundamental freedoms for all without distinction as to race, sex, language, or religion’. Could the Commission accept any form of racially based division of the island, in breach of the European acquis and the principles of the UN Charter?
